text: the lampman's boy has taken over the east street.
a cart came down the high road with no driver. the mule knew the way.
six sacks of meal spoiled in the low store. damp, or rats.
someone left a pair of good boots outside the infirmary door.
the smith is drinking again.
fever in the pit houses. the shifts are short three men.
Pay book, Shaft Four. Tomas Rell, 4 shillings. Tomas Rell, 4 shillings. Tomas Rell, 4 shillings. Tomas Rell, 4 shillings. Tomas Rell, collected by widow. Tomas Rell, 4 shillings.

From the schoolmistress's slate, wiped but not well: The sun is a star. Stars are very far away. Some stars are so far away that we see their light long after they have gone out. Question for tomorrow: how would we know.
Brass lamp, company issue. Dented twice along the left side, as if swung at something low. The wick has been trimmed by someone who cared about it.
Note pinned to the chapel board: Lost, one grey dog, answers to Pepper, three legs, bites. If found please do not bring back, he was never right after the long night, but tell me he is all right.
The old shafts were sealed with stone and mortar and a priest's blessing, and every spring we find the mortar picked clean from the inside.
Grandmother tells the children not to answer if their names are called from the slag heap. She says it the way you would tell them not to touch the stove.
We drew lots for the night watch and Teodor won, which is how we said it then.
The new seam is very rich, the foreman says, and very warm, and we should not mind that it is warm.
The canaries stopped dying in the deep seams. We'd rather they hadn't.
My brother came home from the long shift and kissed our mother and sat in his chair, and she set his place every night after, and every night after the bowl was empty.
The council has resolved that the darkness is temporary. The resolution passed eleven to one, the one being the astronomer, who has been asked to stop bringing his charts.
Nobody likes the cook. Nobody has died of the cook. In the current climate, that counts as a reference.
There is a saying in the valley that every man should leave the world a little brighter than he found it. It was a lot easier to say before.

Mara climbs the lamp post on Pit Street at the first bell and again at the third. It was her husband's post. Thirty-one rungs. She knows which one creaks and steps around it, though there is nobody to wake. When the lamp catches she stays up there a while, longer than the job needs, looking down the street at the other lamps, counting them. Some nights there are fourteen. She climbs down.

The trader stayed four nights. He sold salt and needles and a bolt of yellow cloth that every woman in the valley looked at and nobody could afford. On the fifth morning, if you can call it morning, his cart was gone and so was the Haskett girl. Her mother says she went willingly. Her mother has said it to everyone, twice, without being asked.
